episodes.173395: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed across east central Oklahoma during the late afternoon of the 15th, along a cold front that had become nearly stationary over the area. Additional thunderstorms moved into portions of northeastern and southeastern Oklahoma during the evening. The combination of strong instability and moderately strong deep layer wind shear promoted the development of a few supercell thunderstorms. The strongest thunderstorms produced hail up to quarter size and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.173396: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed across west central Arkansas during the late afternoon of the 15th, along a cold front that had become nearly stationary over the area. Additional thunderstorms moved into the area during the evening. The combination of strong instability and moderately strong deep layer wind shear promoted the development of a few supercell thunderstorms. The strongest thunderstorms produced hail up to ping pong ball size and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.174049: A cold front moved through Arkansas and brought a round of severe thunderstorms with mainly large hail.
episodes.174467: Abundant moisture was drawn north across the region from the 14th into the 15th in advance of a slow moving cold front. Areas of heavy rain lifted north in advance of the front...enhanced by several lows lifting north along the slow moving front. The heaviest rains occurred from the overnight hours of the 14th into the morning of the 15th. Flash flooding developed in both the Bangor/Brewer and Lincoln/Mattawamkeag areas during the early morning hours of the 15th. Numerous roads were closed and impassable due to flash flooding...with vehicles also disabled. Water rescues were also required around Bangor/Brewer with up to 4 feet of standing water reported at some locations. Several roads were also closed in the Lincoln/Mattawamkeag area including Route 155 and Old Military Road. Old Military Road was partially collapsed due to rushing water overwhelming a culvert. Other roads and culverts were also damaged to varying extents across southern and central Penobscot county. Rainfall totals generally ranged from 2.50 to 4.50 inches...with local totals in excess of 5.00 inches.
episodes.174679: A cut-off low pressure system near the Baja Peninsula pulled moisture north into San Bernardino County, and difluence aloft helped trigger thunderstorms. A few storms produced flash flooding.
episodes.174743: With a passing front, showers and a few isolated thunderstorms developed over the Atlantic waters and moved over the east coast in the morning. Enhanced wind shear provided ideal conditions for waterspout development.
episodes.174755: An upper-level low pressure system caused additional rounds of thunderstorms across Southern California on October 15th.
episodes.174780: An approaching polar trough combined with moisture from a stalled frontal system north of the islands resulted in favorable conditions for showers and thunderstorms. Several flooding, mudslides and even hail reports were received.
episodes.174943: Isolated thunderstorms moved rapidly north across southeast Arizona during the afternoon and became more numerous in Pinal County late in the day.  Large hail and damaging winds occurred in southwest Tucson and in rural portions of Pinal County.
episodes.175008: A slow moving low pressure system brought several rounds of showers and thunderstorms across portions of south-central and southwestern Arizona throughout the day on the 15th. Strong southerly flow out ahead of the low pressure system brought in highly anomalous moisture content across the southern half of Arizona, with PWATs surging to 1.1-1.4, which are near record values for mid-October.  Along with the highly anomalous moisture values, moderate to high instability values were also present with MLCAPE rising to 1000-1500 J/KG. Bulk shear values between 25-35 kts were also present. The combination of the highly anomalous moisture content, instability, and shear along with the strong dynamic forcing to the east and north of the low pressure system was a recipe for these showers and thunderstorms to produce flash flooding as well as severe wind gusts and hail. The greatest flash flood impact occurred along portions of western Maricopa County in the area from Buckeye to Tonopah, The greatest damaging wind impact occurred in the Tonopah area, where two rounds of severe thunderstorms, one hour apart, impacted causing widespread power outages due to downed power poles, destroyed two mobile homes, damaged dairy farm structures, and resulted livestock losses. Severe hail was also reported with a storm that moved into the Mesa to Scottsdale area during the overnight period. ||As the area of low pressure moved eastward on the 16th, lingering moisture resulted in the development of more showers and thunderstorms, mainly concentrated across the higher terrain areas east of Phoenix. One isolated storm in particular developed on a open field near Sun Lakes, resulting in the development of a short-lived landspout during the mid-afternoon hours with no damages reported.
episodes.175009: A slow moving low pressure system brought several rounds of showers and thunderstorms across portions of southeast CA, mainly from the late morning through the late afternoon hours. Strong southerly flow out ahead of the low pressure system brought in highly anomalous moisture content across the southern half of Arizona, with PWATs surging to 1.1-1.4, which are near record values for mid-October. Along with the highly anomalous moisture values, moderate to high instability values were also present with MLCAPE rising to 1000-1500 J/KG. Bulk shear values between 25-35 kts were also present. The combination of the highly anomalous moisture content, instability, and shear along with the strong dynamic forcing to the east and north of the low pressure system was a recipe for these showers and thunderstorms to produce flash flooding as well as severe wind gusts and small hail. The area of the greatest impacts occurred across the Imperial Valley, where several reports of flooding along with damaging winds and small hail were received.
episodes.175016: A brief waterspout developed in association with showers and thunderstorms that developed from the interaction of an outflow boundary moving southwest and intersecting a pre-existing convective cumulus cloud line over the Lower Florida Keys.
episodes.175100: Isolated thunderstorms produced hail in the city of Decatur the afternoon of October 15. A complex of thunderstorms produced minor wind damage along the Red River before weakening as it pushed farther south, the night of October 15 into the morning of October 16.
episodes.175396: A stalled out boundary over Central Florida helped to produce strong updrafts resulting in a few hail reports with one reported to be severe.
episodes.175397: A stalled out boundary over Central Florida produced strong thunderstorms over the Gulf of Mexico resulting in strong winds.

events.narrative: Flash flooding developed during the early morning hours of the 15th around the Bangor/Brewer area. Numerous roads were closed and impassable due to the flash flooding. Some water rescues were also required...with standing water up to 4 feet deep in some locations. Several vehicles were also disabled due to the flash flood waters. Some roads and culverts in the area were damaged to varying extents. Rainfall totals with this event generally ranged from 2.50 to 4.50 inches...with local totals in excess of 5.00 inches.

Flash flooding developed during the early morning hours of the 15th. Several roads were impassable and closed due to the flash flooding. Road closures included Route 155 in Enfield along with Old Military Road near Winn. A portion of Old Military Road eventually collapsed due to flash flood waters overwhelming a culvert. Other roads and culverts were damaged to varying extents in the region. Rainfall totals with this event generally ranged from 2.00 to 4.00 inches...with local totals in excess of 4.00 inches.

events.county: Jupiter Inlet To Deerfield Beach Fl Out 20Nm
events.narrative: The public sighted a fully condensed waterspout with a spray ring off Delray Beach. There was a video posted on social media. Time is estimated.

A video showed a significant fire broke out on top of the roof of a home in the area of Happy Valley Road and 95th Avenue in Peoria due to lightning. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.
Thunderstorm winds downed a few trees in Midvale Park in the southwest Tucson metro area. One of the trees fell onto a residence, causing minor damage.

Downed powerlines, 10-15 approximately, reported in the area of Austin Road and West Aten Road in El Centro due to thunderstorm winds. Winds were estimated between 55-60 mph. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.

Image of a large uprooted tree that fell onto a home, resulting in roof damage, in the area of Lenrey Avenue and South 5th Street in El Centro. Winds were estimated between 55-60 mph. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.
Several downed trees were reported across El Centro, with some of the trees falling onto roofs of home. Winds were estimated between 55-60 mph. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.
Power poles, approximately 19, were snapped and spread around the area between El Centro and Calexico. Winds were estimated between 55-60 mph. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.

Several videos showed nuisance flooding across the El Centro area, with vehicles able to traverse through the standing water without any major issues. Water depth was estimated to be 3-5 at most. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
Flooding reported in the area of SR-387 and SR-187 in Sacaton. No damages or injuries were reported.
Social media video taken from Queen Creek showed a significant water current several inches deep flowing in the area just south of the San Tan Mountains. No damages or injuries were reported.
Heavy flooding reported on the on and off ramp of South 4th street and I-8 in El Centro. No damages or injuries were reported.
A trained spotter recorded a 64mph wind gust with a handheld anemometer in the area of East Baseline Road and South Rural Road in Tempe. No damages or injuries were reported.

Significant flooding was reported in the El Centro Regional Medical Center. There was 18 inches of flowing water in the parking lot, with the water entering the facility and affecting the emergency room as well as the radiology department. No injuries were reported.
A powerline and possibly a power pole were blown down by thunderstorm winds in the area of SR-115 & Titsworth Road in Calipatria. Winds were estimated between 55-60 mph. No injuries were reported.
Ping pong ball sized hail was reported about a mile south of Nimrod Lake.

A Trained Spotter sent pictures of a couple of trees, with branches snapped, along with a large uprooted tree that fell onto an SUV causing some damage to the vehicle near the Love Truck Stop Station located just south of I-10 in Tolleson. TPHX terminal doppler radar measured over 70 mph in the area. No injuries were reported.
A Yuma Proving Ground Station measured a 68 mph wind gust.
Lake Cuyamaca received 1.59 inches of rain in hour, occurring between 1 and 2 PM local time. The storm total rainfall as of 7 AM local time on the 16th was 2.78 inches.

A 12 year old girl, who lives in the Sun City West Retirement Community, was struck by lightning while playing outside, causing her heart to stop. Her father was able to successfully resuscitate her. The girl was taken to the hospital afterwards. Timing of the lightning strike was estimated by radar.
Flooding reported on I-17 near Bell Road in Phoenix. No damages or injuries were reported.
A mesonet station at Senator Wash measured a 71 mph wind gust.
Plows from the California Highway Patrol removed flood debris from SR-111 near Milepost 65. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.
Flooding reported on US-95 near Milepost 104 in Quartzsite. No damages or injuries were reported.

Video from a storm chaser showed flash flooding washing away Mohave Road. The location of the flooding was about 6-7 miles north of I-10, just northeast of Blythe, CA. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.
A trained spotter reported quarter sized hail just east of the Hwy. 31 and 38 intersection.
A trained spotter measured spiky hail that was 2 inches in diameter.
Three to four feet of water accumulated on Box Canyon Road at Coachella Canal Road. Boulders were also in the road, causing Box Canyon Road to close at 4:45 PM local time.

Emergency managers reported flooding at Sector Los Cocos in Barrio Marias in Moca due to excessive rainfall. Rio Culebrinas, nearby, was also out of its banks. Some low-water crossings were impassable.
Social media video of hail just W of I-75 and S of SR-70. Several other social media videos showing hail around this time in the same area. Time from video stamp.

events.county: Gulf Of Mexico From West End Of Seven Mile Bridge To Halfmoon Shoal Out To 5 Fathoms
events.narrative: A brief, narrow waterspout was observed to the west-northwest of Key West.  The condensation funnel cloud was tilted at a nearly 45-degree angle and drifting slowly toward the west.  The funnel cloud extended one third the way to the horizon.
Pictures on social media showed golfball sized hail east of Cabot, south of Austin.
Water flowed down Utah Trail.
Emergency management reported moderate flow of water down Utah Trail located in the northwestern portion of Joshua Tree National Park. No damages or injuries were reported.
Water running along the eastbound lanes of I-10 resulted in closure of the highway near Ford Dry Lake Road. No damages or injuries were reported.
A trained spotter reported nickel sized hail in Decatur, TX.
Strong thunderstorm wind blew down power lines.
Hail up to ping pong ball size damaged homes and vehicles.
Strong thunderstorm wind snapped power poles.
Large rocks and boulders washed onto Amboy Rd.
Hail up to half dollar size damaged homes and vehicles.
Thunderstorm wind gusts were estimated to 60 mph.
Strong thunderstorm wind snapped large tree limbs.
Dirt, debris, and rocks on Palowet Drive at Highway 74.
